comments: I already have a recent master's in Writing Studies and Educational Psychology with a 4.0 GPA, as well as over a decade of social work experience, and several academic publications, conference presentations, and workshops that focused on therapeutic techniques, mental wellbeing, or disability. I also taught for my entire master's degree, was an Assistant Director of the Writing Center, and conducted my own 100+ participant study. I was waitlisted on March 30th, told all decisions would be final by April 24th, and then received an email offering me admission into the part-time and non-funded 3-year program (rather than the full-time, funded 2-year program I had applied for) on April 29th. I was told within the next week I would get my official offer of admission, and I had that same one week to accept it and pay the $250 admission fee. I emailed back 6 days later saying I had discussed with my support network and had decided to reject the offer due to national instability and uncertainty of gov financial aid, but would like to reapply in the future. I asked how to indicate this acceptance on a potential future application, as I had never received an official admission offer. Two weeks after that, I got my official admission offer and a host of emails telling me what my next steps were. All of them had inconsistent and contradictory information, including dates that were different email to email and deadlines that had passed weeks ago. One email had three different dates for the same (important) deadline. I finally got a response to the email I had sent directly to the Admissions Office, saying they were sorry to hear I was declining and informing me of the steps I needed to take to officially decline. They did not answer the other questions I had included in my email to them. Throughout all of this, my name was only spelled correctly once. We will see if I do end up reapplying in future years.

comments: Early Nov 2025 contacted potential supervisor and was encouraged to apply, end of Nov 2025 submitted application, mid Jan 2026 submitted application for L4E fellowship. Early Feb 2026 I get a Whatsapp message from my proposed secondary supervisor on a Sunday afternoon (Montreal time) asking if I'm available in the next couple of hours to discuss my application. As an international applicant in a different time zone unfortunately I was already asleep so replied first thing on Monday morning trying to arrange a time we could talk, and was told they would get back to me with a different time. The next thing I hear is on the 21st April when I get sent an email to look at the application portal where I find a generic rejection message. In the mean time I sent numerous follow up messages asking if they still wanted to talk with me but I never got a reply. McGill's website suggested that most applicants would hear back at the end of February and throughout March so towards the end of March I began to reach out by email to the proposed primary supervisor, program administrator, and L4E to see if they could give me any insight into the progress of my application or when I could expect to hear back. These emails and subsequent follow ups were also all completely ignored. I am obviously gutted about my application being rejected however given the seeming distinct lack of compassion, communication, and organisation shown by the anthropology department at McGill and the L4E it raises some major red flags to me about the quality of teaching and support that is offered by both the program and the fellowship. I would be very interested to hear from successful applicants about if this is the case? If the other applications I am still waiting on are also unsuccessful I will be applying for PhD programs again next year, however given the inadequacy of my experience this year I shan't be reapplying to McGill. Very disappointed.

comments: No interview, and to be honest, I didn't stand a chance. Contacting supervisors beforehand was (and is) recommended, so I had established contact with a PI in Sep '25, who asked me to check in again in Q1 '26 for possible PhD and/or MSc by Research positions (I am in my final year of undergrad). I followed up with them twice in early Jan '26 (since the deadline was Jan 15), but didn't get a response. I knew it was a lost cause because I could see on LinkedIn that they were deeply, DEEPLY invested in industrial research, consulting, and other roles outside of academia. It's not a bad thing, but it certainly is worth keeping in mind. I applied anyway since I had an excellent fit with their research directions and had already sent TOEFL/GRE scores to the program. This rejection was always coming. Anyway, I have accepted another top-tier offer from elsewhere, so it doesn't matter anymore. But to anyone reading this: please do not, DO NOT apply to NUS ECE without explicit PI interest, especially if you're thinking of doing so straight out of undergrad.

comments: I had a very disappointing experience applying to the PhD program in EECS at the University of Wyoming. I submitted my application in January and never received any clear communication regarding its completeness. There were no notifications about missing documents, and every time I reached out for a status update, I received vague or delayed responses. In several instances, there was no reply at all. The lack of professionalism from the department, including the Graduate Coordinator, was frustrating. As an applicant investing significant time, effort, and money into the process, I expected at least basic transparency and communication. Unfortunately, that standard was not met. What makes this worse is that the final rejection cited multiple concerns, but none of these were ever communicated earlier in the process, nor was there any opportunity to clarify or strengthen the application. It raises serious questions about how thoroughly applications are handled and whether they are reviewed in a timely and organized manner. Overall, the experience felt disorganized, dismissive, and disrespectful toward applicants. Based on this experience, I would strongly caution prospective students to think carefully before applying here. Applicants deserve timely communication, clear guidance, and professional treatment—none of which I experienced in this process.

Dear BAH BAH BAH,
I am writing in regard to your application for admission to graduate study at the
University of Southern California. After careful review of your application and
supporting materials, the Admission Committee has asked me to inform you that we are
unable to offer you admission to the Doctor of Philosophy program in Media Arts and
Practice for Fall 2026.
We understand this must be very disappointing news. Please bear in mind that each year
the university receives applications from many more students than it can accommodate.
Admissibility is determined by the size of the applicant pool as well as student
credentials. Unfortunately, as a result we are not able to offer admission to some
students of significant ability and potential.
We encourage you to continue to work toward your educational and professional goals,
and wish you every success in your future endeavors.
Sincerely,
you.usc.edu
Timothy E. Brunold
Dean of Admission

comments:
First notification was in the portal with a two sentence rejection notice. Several days later I received an email with a more detailed explanation:  

"The Graduate Admissions Committee in the Department of English at the University of Florida has completed its review of applications and, unfortunately, has not selected you for admission.
 
This is no reflection on your academic excellence. We received more than 200 applications from talented and accomplished students all over the world for our graduate program, and we have admitted fewer than 10%. With so many excellent applicants to choose from, our decisions often came down to judgments about which students we can best support with our particular faculty expertise, our library resources, and the teaching and other training opportunities we can provide. Many of those who applied to our program can, we believe, actually be served better elsewhere. We hope that you get that opportunity, and we wish you luck and success in your future endeavors.
 
One final note: because we had so many applicants, we are unable to offer each applicant a detailed response on our Admissions Committee’s decision. Thank you for considering the University of Florida and for giving us an opportunity to review your materials. We are always amazed and humbled by the astonishing work that applicants to our program intend to do in the future. This year is no exception."

comments: I presume it's a rejection, anyway, because surely "hmm we're struggling to figure out how to make the system display the details ... check tomorrow" is not what they'd choose for acceptances and waitlists.  I feel for the person I'm in email contact with, who sounds unsupported in their job (which perhaps also happened in 2024 if you look back in these results?).  I emailed asking when I might get my decision because it seems late.  They emailed back very promptly saying it should be in the portal.  I responded that when I log in to ApplyWeb, on the page where I can see all the universities that used ApplyWeb, there is a "decision letter" button above the "checklist" button but this doesn't appear for Cornell.  They responded that perhaps it needs to process overnight, but let them know if I still didn't see it tomorrow.  I talked to the tech support bot which suggests (Interesting to know!) that universities load a bunch of decision letters and then have to add a date and time and give permission for the student to view it (so if the college says it's there and I say it's not, they probably didn't give permission yet).  I sent that info to the kind administrative person at Cornell's History Graduate program, who thanked me for it and said it gave them an idea of a few things to go check.  Sounds like the funding cuts really hit a lot of areas -- my home department has had a lot of cuts and it's our admin person who is bearing the brunt of a lot of it.  Anyway.  Still can't see a decision in the portal, but it's apparent my application is just an administrative loose end, and this cycle has taught me that my research niche is "weird" and difficult for programs to find space for.  1a/7r/3p is I think the current tally, one pending is a Public Policy program.

Dear Applicant,
Thank you for the time, effort, and passion you put into your application to the UCSC Physics graduate program. There is a person behind every application, statement of purpose, and letter of recommendation, and we truly appreciate the effort you contributed applying to our program. That is what makes it challenging to inform you we are unable to recommend you for admission for this coming fall.

This was a difficult decision for our committee for two reasons: 1) this year’s applicant pool was exceptionally talented, and the level of research experience and academic dedication we saw was genuinely humbling; and 2) due to department funding and faculty research capacity we are simply unable to recommend offers of admission to all researchers we believe would thrive here.

This decision is a reflection of our departmental constraints, not a reflection of your potential as a physicist. There are many paths towards scientific inquiry, and we hope you continue pursuing your interests in physics research.

Understandably, many applicants ask us for feedback on their applications to see how they can improve in the future. Please understand due to the sheer number of requests we receive the committee is unable to provide comment on any individual's application. We trust that your continued efforts and dedication will open doors for you as you pursue your career.

Thank you again for considering UC Santa Cruz. We wish you the very best in your next chapter.

comments:
Email from DGS. Honestly thought the interview went well, and it was my top choice, which makes it even harder. That said, I have to give them credit: it's probably the kindest and most considerate rejection letter I've ever received, acknowledging the time and effort applicants put in. Still sad, but grateful for the thoughtful note.

"...Applying to graduate school takes significant energy and time, and we were honored that you included us among your choices for application. While we aren’t able to offer specific feedback on your application, please know that our decision this year is not a negative evaluation of your suitability for graduate school or a career in the history profession. Each year, we must forego the opportunity to work with and learn from many talented applicants. The loss is entirely ours, and we hope that you will find another path where you will be supported to pursue your passions."

comments:
I received an email from the Director of the Doctoral Program congratulating me on my admission and providing the letter of admission with the full details of my offer. An additional email from the graduate school with full details is supposed to follow shortly. I received full funding for five years for 12 month/year including a minimum stipend of $43k annually and was also given details about additional funding resources through the program and graduate school.
A few more details to share: prior to applying, I did not contact my intended advisors to talk about applying. Also, I did not receive an interview request prior to receiving admission. I was accepted without any direct contact between myself and my intended advisors through my whole process of application.
I have a year of previous ethnographic fieldwork, over a decade of life experience in the context I want to work in, years of professional experience in social research methods, two master's degrees with GPAs of 3.6, and some slight professional connections to my intended advisors (mostly through my past professors who are acquaintances with them). Strong “fit” with my intended advisors and a good SOP was key, I think, in my admission.

Due to the large number of applications we received, we are not able to provide individual feedback on Committee decisions.

Please accept my best wishes for your future, and I hope you will find the perfect fit at another Ph.D. program.

With best wishes

The professors at this institution showed such enthusiasm for me and my work that it is without a doubt the right fit; Find you a school that is excited about you as you are it. I think program fit is the most important part, I'm realizing. I haven't gotten rejections / any kind of decision from other places yet, but I have already informally accepted U-Mich and will most definitely be attending there. I found that you have to find the program that really fits your needs and goals, and then things tend to fall into place. I never thought they would. Best of luck to everyone.

I am pleased to invite you to attend our University of Washington Bioengineering Department Visit from March 12-14th in Seattle, WA.

 

During your visit, you will have the opportunity to meet with our faculty and graduate students, tour UW laboratories and campus facilities, and learn more about life in Seattle and the Pacific Northwest.

 

For candidates residing outside the Seattle metropolitan area, the Department will cover the cost of a round-trip economy flight, provide a $400 lodging stipend, and cover most meals during your visit. Please note that candidates are responsible for any airfare or seat upgrades, luggage fees, and transportation to and from their home/departure airport. Local candidates may apply for a $150 transportation stipend to help offset mileage, parking, or related expenses.

 

Unfortunately, the department is not able to host candidates at an alternative time.

 

Our goal is to offer funding packages to all accepted PhD students. To ensure we can offer the most comprehensive and accurate funding packages, admission and funding offers will be decided shortly after this visit event. While attendance at our campus visit is not mandatory to be considered for funding, an in-person visit is crucial to ensure prospective students are well acquainted with our department, and that our faculty are well acquainted with our prospective students.

waitlist for the MFA Program in Creative Writing at The Ohio State University. All of us on the faculty here
greatly admire your work and would be delighted to have you with us next year should a spot open. 

The truth is, determining “who gets in” versus “who gets waitlisted” once we have agreed on a group of writers
we want to admit is always ridiculously difficult. This is an inexact business (and of course it’s not a “business”
at all), and ours is a very small program by design. Please be aware that you are among a distinguished group of
writers who received enthusiastic “yes” votes from every one of the relevant faculty. 

I can promise you that the very latest you will hear from us about your admission will be one week after April
15, which is the date by which all admitted students must either decline or accept our offer. It’s very possible
that you will hear from us sooner, but I wouldn’t count on that, as many people wait until the last possible
minute to say yes or no. All I can tell you for sure is that as soon as we know how many offers have been
accepted, I will contact you one way or the other.
